outcomes.text: 'That's my car. He bought it.' The others go quiet. They all have cars.

choices.label: "This is triangulation. I'm leaving the triangle."
choices.receipt: You named his tactic and walked out.

outcomes.text: The therapist's word lands like a slap. He has no answer. You leave with your dignity and his pepper soup.

beats.text: 7am. Banging on the door. Two men with a court order.
We're here for Chief Emeka's assets. The Prado is on the list. So is this TV.
Babe... talk to them. You have a good face.
{tell}

broke.text: Outside, a tow truck is already hooking the Prado. A CAR HIRE man is shouting at it.

choices.label: Talk to them. Charm. Lie.
choices.receipt: You lied to the bailiffs for him.

outcomes.text: They leave with only the TV. Chief kisses your forehead: 'My lucky charm.'
They take the TV, the Prado, and your phone charger.

choices.label: Ask the bailiffs how much he owes
choices.receipt: You asked the bailiffs how much he owes.

outcomes.text: '₦47 million, madam. Plus interest. Plus the Prado.'

choices.label: "Refund my container money. Now."
choices.receipt: You demanded your money back as the bailiffs watched.

outcomes.text: He transfers it back before the bailiffs finish the list. Fastest he's ever moved.
'Babe. They froze my account.' For once, he's telling the truth.

choices.label: Show the bailiffs the papers you signed
choices.receipt: You showed the bailiffs the papers you'd signed.

outcomes.text: They photograph your signature. 'You're the guarantor, madam. See you in court.'

choices.label: Livestream the eviction to the Parlour
choices.receipt: You livestreamed his eviction.

outcomes.text: 12,000 viewers. Chief tries to hide behind the fridge. The fridge is also on the list.

beats.text: A woman in expensive lace at your door. Two kids behind her.
I'm Nkechi. Emeka's wife. For the children's sake, we should talk.
{tell}

divorced.text: Her ring finger has the same pale band as his.

choices.label: Let her in. Make tea. Listen.
choices.receipt: You let her in and listened.

outcomes.text: Two hours. The divorce in 2022. The weekends with the kids. He wasn't hiding you. He was hiding his pain.

choices.label: Slam the door. Post her on the Parlour.
choices.receipt: You posted his ex-wife on the Parlour.

outcomes.text: The Parlour eats it up. Then Nkechi posts the divorce certificate. You posted an ex-wife.

choices.label: Call Chief on speaker. "Explain. Now."
choices.receipt: You called Chief on speaker in front of her.

outcomes.text: He arrives in 20 minutes, shirt untucked. 'She's my ex. I should have told you. I was ashamed.'

choices.label: "Is she why you have two phones?"
choices.receipt: You asked about the second phone.

outcomes.text: Nkechi laughs. 'The second phone is for the children. So I can't reach him at weekends. Smart man.'

beats.text: A DM from a stranger.
That watch in your post. Gold Daytona, scratched bezel. I know that watch. Whose wrist is it?
{tell}

serial_sponsor.text: Her profile picture is cropped. You can just see a gold bracelet.

broke.text: Her bio: 'Import finance. Apapa. DM for clearing.'

divorced.text: Her profile: a woman in lace with two kids. The same voice from his phone.

choices.label: "My man's. Jealous?"
choices.receipt: You told a stranger the Rolex was your man's.

outcomes.text: She replies with one eye emoji. Then screenshots your profile.

choices.label: Delete the post. Block the stranger.
choices.receipt: You deleted the post and blocked the stranger.

outcomes.text: Deleted. But the internet has a long memory and a short temper.

choices.label: "Why do you know it?"
choices.receipt: You asked the stranger how she knew the watch.

outcomes.text: No reply.

serial_sponsor.text: 'Because my sister has the same video. Different date. Same table.'

broke.text: 'Because it was pawned at my uncle's shop in Ikeja last month. Somebody redeemed it on credit.'

divorced.text: 'Because I bought it for him. Long story. Tell him Nkechi says hi.'

beats.text: Voice note, 0:47. Unknown number.
You. The one with the watch video. We need to talk about Emeka. Admiralty Way, 4pm. Come alone.

choices.label: Meet her at the salon
choices.receipt: You met the woman from the voice note.

outcomes.text: She doesn't show.

serial_sponsor.text: His wife. Calm. Terrifying. She hands you a list: 'You're number four. I have the other three addresses too.'

broke.text: A businesswoman. 'He owes me ₦12m. Help me find his assets and I'll cut you in.'

divorced.text: His ex-wife. 'I'm not here to fight. I'm here to warn you: he works too much and he snores. Good luck.'

choices.label: Forward the voice note to Chief
choices.receipt: You forwarded the voice note to Chief.

outcomes.text: He reads it. Says nothing.

serial_sponsor.text: He calls in 30 seconds. 'Delete it. Delete her. I'll send something.' He sends something.

broke.text: 'Don't meet her. She's trying to ruin me.' She is. He also owes her.

divorced.text: 'That's Nkechi. My ex. I'm sorry she found you. I'll explain everything Sunday.'

choices.label: Block her. Not your wahala.
choices.receipt: You blocked the woman without listening.

outcomes.text: Blocked. She'll find another way. They always find another way.

beats.text: You leaked that woman's rant. To the Parlour. With my name in it. Explain.

choices.label: "It wasn't me. Lagos has eyes."
choices.receipt: You denied leaking the rant.

outcomes.text: He wants to believe you, so he does.
He shows you the upload: your phone model, your ring light, your voice saying 'omo'.

choices.label: "She came for me. I defended myself."
choices.receipt: You told him you were defending yourself.

outcomes.text: He's quiet across the whole bridge. 'Next time, come to me first.'

choices.label: "And I'll do it again."
choices.receipt: You told him you'd leak it again.

outcomes.text: Musa stops the car. Chief gets out. Walks. On the Link Bridge. In agbada.

beats.text: Good morning, ma. You're guarantor on a defaulted facility. ₦18 million. When can you come in?

choices.label: Hang up. Block. Pray.
choices.receipt: You hung up on the bank.

outcomes.text: They call your office line next. Then your mother.

choices.label: Pay a lawyer to fight it
choices.receipt: You paid a lawyer to fight the guarantor claim.

outcomes.text: Your lawyer gets your name removed: 'signed under misrepresentation'. Chief is not invited to your birthday.

choices.label: Call Chief: "Guarantor? GUARANTOR?"
choices.receipt: You called Chief about the guarantor loan.

outcomes.text: 'Babe, it's a formality.' The bank officer is still on the other line, listening.

beats.text: I told you. Don't touch my phones. You did. So: what did you find?

choices.label: "Enough." Hold his stare.
choices.receipt: You told him you found enough.

outcomes.text: He blinks first. Then he sends ₦200k. Sorry money, or shut-up money. Same app.

good_one.text: 'Then you found my kids' school WhatsApp. Happy?' He goes to bed without you.

choices.label: "Nothing. I'm sorry. I panicked."
choices.receipt: You apologised for going through his phone.

outcomes.text: He nods slowly. 'Trust is not a phone password.' He keeps both phones on him now.

choices.label: "Give me your password. Fair is fair."
choices.receipt: You demanded his password.

outcomes.text: He laughs once. It is not a happy laugh. 'Goodnight.'

beats.text: Unknown number. A photo: you, cap low, leaving the salon. Caption:
I know your face now.

choices.label: "And I know your husband's."
choices.receipt: You clapped back at the woman with your photo.

outcomes.text: Three dots. For eleven minutes. Then she adds you to a WhatsApp group called 'EMEKA MATTER'.

divorced.text: 'Ex-husband. Keep him. Return the Rolex.' She leaves the group she just created.

choices.label: Screenshot it. Say nothing. Change your route.
choices.receipt: You stayed silent and changed your route.

outcomes.text: You take the BRT for a week. Disguised. It's the most Lagos you've ever felt.

choices.label: Send it to Chief: "Your wife has my face."
choices.receipt: You sent Chief the photo his wife had of you.

outcomes.text: 'I'll handle her.' He doesn't say how. That's the scary part.

divorced.text: 'That's Nkechi. My EX. I'll call her.' He does. She stops.

beats.text: A driver you don't know is at your gate. A card in gold ink:
Tea. Ikoyi. Four o'clock. Come and see the family you're trying to join.

choices.label: Go, with a cake. Manners first.
choices.receipt: You took a cake to tea with Chief's first wife.

outcomes.text: She inspects you like a new hire. 'Rooms are allocated by seniority. You'd be number three.' The second wife refills your tea without a word.

choices.label: Send the driver back. You don't do summons.
choices.receipt: You refused the first wife's summons.

outcomes.text: The driver shrugs. The card stays on your table like a threat with good handwriting.
Next morning the same driver is outside your office. With your boss.

choices.label: Call Chief: "Your wife has summoned me."
choices.receipt: You told Chief his wife had summoned you.

outcomes.text: 'Don't go! She'll poison your mind.' Then: 'Wear the green one if you do.'

beats.text: Share your live location with me. Always. I pay for this phone. I should know where it is.
He's smiling. His hand is on your phone.

choices.label: Share it. He's just protective.
choices.receipt: You shared your live location with him. Permanently.

outcomes.text: He kisses your forehead. Your phone feels heavier.

choices.label: "No. My location is mine."
choices.receipt: You told him your location is yours.

outcomes.text: The AC hums. Musa drives very carefully. Chief says nothing for the rest of the bridge.

choices.label: "Let me think." Call your Bestie from the toilet.
choices.receipt: You called your Bestie when he pushed for your location.

outcomes.text: Bestie: 'Is he paying for the phone or for you?' You don't share it.

choices.label: "Day one: I share location with friends. Not owners."
choices.receipt: You reminded him of your day-one location rule.

outcomes.text: He remembers. You see him remember. He takes his hand off your phone.

choices.label: "Musa, stop the car." Get out. Leave.
choices.receipt: You got out of the Prado and left.

outcomes.text: You walk off the bridge and into a keke. You don't look back.

beats.text: 2am. You wake up. Chief is sitting at the end of your bed in the dark.
I have a key. I wanted to see you sleep. Is that a crime?

choices.label: Make him tea. He's had a long day.
choices.receipt: You made him tea at 2am instead of asking why he was there.

outcomes.text: He drinks it watching you. 'This is what love looks like,' he says. You nod. You don't sleep.

choices.label: "Give me the key. Now."
choices.receipt: You took back the key.

outcomes.text: He puts it on the bedside table. Slowly. Like it costs him. It does.

choices.label: Call estate security. Then your sister.
choices.receipt: You called estate security on him.

outcomes.text: The security man knocks. Chief leaves, offended. Your sister stays on the phone till sunrise.

choices.label: "You said this flat was mine."
choices.receipt: You reminded him he said the flat was yours.

outcomes.text: 'It is yours. And you are mine.' He says it like maths.

choices.label: Pack one bag. Leave before sunrise.
choices.receipt: You packed a bag and left before sunrise.

outcomes.text: You leave the keys on the marble. The first danfo at Obalende has never sounded so good.

beats.text: Give me your phone. Unlock it. I want to see who you talk to when I'm not there.
The man who said 'never touch my phones' is holding out his hand.

choices.label: Hand it over. Nothing to hide.
choices.receipt: You unlocked your phone for him.

outcomes.text: He reads for twenty minutes. Deletes two contacts. Hands it back: 'Good.'

choices.label: "No. Same rule as yours."
choices.receipt: You refused to unlock your phone.

outcomes.text: He stares. You stare. The waiter decides to come back later.

choices.label: "This is control. My therapist has a word for it."
choices.receipt: You named his control out loud.

outcomes.text: Hearing it named, he looks smaller. Not sorry. Smaller.

choices.label: Put your phone in your bag. Walk out.
choices.receipt: You walked out of the restaurant.

outcomes.text: You take the stairs, not the lift. Faster. You order a ride on the phone he wanted.

beats.text: Babe, how was your day? Mine was long. Don't call me around 6pm, I'm always in meetings. Talk later, sweet.

choices.label: "Noted: 6pm is meeting time 😌"
choices.receipt: You noted his 6pm rule.

outcomes.text: 'Sharp.' He sends a heart. You've just learned his schedule.

choices.label: "Miss you already 🥺"
choices.receipt: You sent him a 'miss you'.

outcomes.text: He sends three hearts and a ₦10k 'for airtime'.

choices.label: "Long day? Send something for my long day too."
choices.receipt: You asked him to send money for your long day.

outcomes.text: ₦20k lands. No message. Efficient.

beats.text: My boys want to take me to some seafood place in VI. I hate seafood places. The smell. Anyway, what are you eating?

choices.label: "Then suya. Always suya. Never seafood."
choices.receipt: You caught that he hates seafood.

outcomes.text: 'You understand me.' He sends a suya emoji. Then another.

choices.label: Send a picture of your noodles
choices.receipt: You sent him a picture of your noodles.

outcomes.text: 'Noodles?! Ah. Send account number.' ₦15k.

choices.label: "Lobster, obviously. Treat me."
choices.receipt: You asked him for lobster.

outcomes.text: He leaves you on read for an hour.

beats.text: Musa will pick you up tomorrow. Musa is the only man in Lagos I trust. If Musa says it, it's true.

choices.label: "Musa is the source of truth. Got it."
choices.receipt: You caught that Musa never lies.

outcomes.text: 'Exactly.' He doesn't realise what he just gave you.

choices.label: "And me? Do you trust me?"
choices.receipt: You asked if he trusts you.

outcomes.text: 'Small small.' Honest, at least.

choices.label: "Send money for Uber instead."
choices.receipt: You asked for Uber money instead of Musa.

outcomes.text: ₦8k arrives. Musa arrives anyway.

beats.text: Good morning. My mother's birthday is Saturday. She likes people who greet properly. Unlike my nephews. Anyway. Breakfast?

choices.label: "Tell Mama I said happy early birthday 🎉"
choices.receipt: You remembered his mother's birthday.

outcomes.text: 'She will like you.' A pause. 'I like you.'

choices.label: "Breakfast? Send for akara."
choices.receipt: You asked him for akara money.

outcomes.text: ₦5k for akara. He's laughing. You can hear it.

choices.label: Reply with a sleeping emoji
choices.receipt: You replied with a sleeping emoji.

outcomes.text: He sends one too. Romance is dead. Long live romance.

beats.text: Busy day. I sign nothing without my lawyer, Barrister Okafor. That's how you survive Lagos. Remember that.

choices.label: "Barrister Okafor. Noted. Wise man."
choices.receipt: You noted his lawyer's name.

outcomes.text: 'Very wise.' He means himself.

choices.label: "Too busy for me? 🙄"
choices.receipt: You complained he was too busy.

outcomes.text: He sends a voice note apologising for 4 minutes. It has a car horn in it.

choices.label: "Survive Lagos? Help me survive this week."
choices.receipt: You asked him to help you survive the week.

outcomes.text: ₦25k. 'Survive small.'

beats.text: Heads up. From Friday evening my phone will be off. Family things. It's not you. Don't overthink it, eh?

choices.label: "Friday is family. I won't call."
choices.receipt: You promised not to call him on Fridays.

outcomes.text: 'Thank you.' Two words. He sounds relieved.

choices.label: "Which family, Chief?"
choices.receipt: You asked him which family.

outcomes.text: He sends a laughing emoji. Only a laughing emoji.

choices.label: "Okay sha. Send weekend money."
choices.receipt: You asked for weekend money.

outcomes.text: ₦30k. 'Enjoy your weekend.' Your weekend. Not ours.
